transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well... I guess I'm just having a hard time slowing down. It feels like I’m constantly running on a motor lately. I'll finish one thing at school, or around the house, and... I just immediately jump right into the next thing. I can't really seem to shut myself off. That's mostly it.
Have you noticed any change in your sleep lately, like feeling rested even if you haven't slept much?
No... not really. I sleep about the same as always. If I don't get enough sleep, I'm tired, so... no, I haven't noticed anything like that.
Have you had any periods where your mood was unusually high, euphoric, or irritable, lasting at least a few days?
No... I haven't noticed anything like that. My mood is just... normal, I guess. I don't really get euphoric or anything. Just restless, like I said.

Have you ever had a period where you felt down most of the day, lost interest in things you usually enjoy, or had other symptoms like changes in appetite, trouble concentrating, or thoughts that life isn’t worth living?
No... I don't think so. I don't really get down like that. My appetite is fine, and... no, no thoughts like that. Just what I mentioned before.
Have you been more active than usual, like doing a lot of things at once or feeling like you can't sit still?
Not more than usual, no. I mean... I always have trouble sitting still. It's not some new thing. Just... how I am.
Have you experienced any periods where you felt you needed less sleep than usual, like you could function well with very little sleep?
No, I don't think so. I sleep about the same as I always do. Nothing out of the ordinary there.
Have you ever had a time when your mood was noticeably different from usual—like feeling unusually excited, overly confident, or easily annoyed—for several days in a row?
No... not really. I mean, I get annoyed sometimes, like anyone else, but... no, not for days in a row or anything like that. Just my normal self.
Have you had any distinct periods where you felt unusually energetic or driven to accomplish goals, even if it wasn’t something you normally care about?
No... I don't think so. I just do what I need to do. I don't really get phases like that.
Have you noticed your thoughts feeling unusually fast or racing, like you can't quite keep up with them?
No, I wouldn't say that. My thoughts just... move at a normal pace, I guess. Nothing like that.
Do you often find it hard to focus or stay attentive, especially when doing tasks that require sustained mental effort, like schoolwork or chores?
No... not really. I mean, I get my work done. I don't think I have a problem paying attention when I need to.
Have there been times when you felt a strong inner restlessness or pressure to keep moving or doing things, more than your usual self?

Yeah... I suppose so. That's actually kind of what brought me in. I just feel like... I'm constantly running on a motor lately. Like, I finish one thing at school, or at home, and I just immediately jump into the next thing. I just... can't really shut myself off.
How long have you been feeling this inner restlessness or pressure to keep moving? Has it been going on for at least a month?
Yeah... longer than a month. I'd say it's been about eight months. Just... around the time we had an older relative move in with us.
Is this inner restlessness or pressure to keep moving something that you experience most of the day, nearly every day?
Yeah. I guess... most days. Just kind of always there.
Has this inner restlessness or pressure to keep moving caused you any significant problems in school, with friends, or at home?

Yes... it has. At work, I mean. The complaints got bad enough that they put me on a corrective plan. And at home... my wife says it's just harder to manage the caregiving routines now. Like they have to manage my energy on top of everything else. I just... I feel like I'm damaging trust with everyone, even though I'm just trying to help.
Does this inner restlessness happen in all situations — like at home, at work, and when you're out in public — or is it more noticeable in certain places or around certain people?
I don't... I'm not really sure. I guess it just happens wherever. I haven't really paid attention to if it's worse in certain places.
Have you noticed yourself fidgeting, pacing, or being unable to relax physically, even if you wanted to?

Yeah... I suppose so. Like... if I'm in an IEP meeting at school, or my admin classes. I guess my leg is usually bouncing under the table. Or I'll be clicking a pen, just shifting in the chair a lot. I don't really notice it at first... usually I only realize I'm doing it because people start glancing over at me.

When you feel that inner restlessness or pressure to keep moving, does it usually come along with feeling worried, tense, or on edge, or does it seem to happen more on its own without that anxious feeling?
I don't... I haven't really thought about it like that. I don't think I feel worried, exactly. It just... it's just there. It happens on its own, I guess.

Do you notice that this restlessness or pressure to keep moving happens even when there’s no particular stress or pressure going on, or does it usually only come up when something specific is bothering you?
I don't know. I guess it just... happens. I haven't really noticed if something's bothering me or not. It's just kind of always there.
